messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary p99 latency breach for /v1/chat (model: rwd-bert-v3.2-canary). p99=7.2s, p95=1.8s — SLO=500ms. Triggered.
alex: I'm on it. Jumping to dashboards now — https://console.redwood.ai/insights/canary/rwd-bert-v3.2
rachel: I see streaming stalls on canary pods; tail logs show repeated "kvcache miss" spikes and stalled chunk flushes. Affects us-west1 and us-east1.
luis: Confirmed. GPU utilization is low (~60%) on affected pods while latency spikes — smells like a kernel fallback or bad compilation.
alex: Can we immediately reduce canary weight to 0? I can update routing.
alex: Running:
```
redwood route update --model rwd-bert-v3.2-canary --weight 0
kubectl -n inference set env ds canary-routers TRAFFIC_WEIGHT=0
```
oncall-bot: alex reduced canary weight to 0 at 14:09 UTC; traffic shift in progress (est ~30s).
rachel: Also enabling fallback model for streaming endpoints:
```
PATCH /v1/config/fallback
{ "route": "/v1/chat", "fallback_model": "rwd-bert-v3.1-stable" }
```
devops: Question — do we want to scale the canary pool while rollback happens? `dedicated scale --pool canary --replicas 6`
luis: I don't recommend scaling; that could increase exposure. Keep weight 0 and drain existing canary sessions.
alex: Watching traces. p95 back to ~600ms after weight->0, p99 still ~2.1s for a few minutes.
product-oncall: Any 5xxs or customer errors? CS reported two customers noticed streaming stalls and client-side timeouts (30s). No 500s in our logs yet.
rachel: No 500s, just large tail latencies and stalled streaming chunks. Adding logs/trace snapshots to incident doc.
sre-lead: Create an incident page and assign severity. @alex @rachel take triage, @luis investigate model artifact/compile.
alex: Created incident INC-20260215-17, severity P1. Customer impact: degraded streaming for ~12% of canary traffic, no full outage.
oncall-handoff: I'm on in 20m. Current actions: weight->0 (done), rollback if p99 > 1.5s after 10m, collecting heap/traces from canary pods.
customer-success: Messaging to affected customers drafted: "We're investigating intermittent streaming delays affecting a small subset of traffic. Fallbacks are in place. We'll update within 30 minutes."
rachel: Found probable root cause: automatic kernel selection chose a slower matmul kernel for the int8 quantized path on certain cards/drivers. Repro locally with same driver and quantization flags. Filing bug CL-5472.
luis: Mitigation suggestion: pin quantization/compilation profile to the v3.1 behavior and re-run model compile; longer-term fix in kernel selector.
alex: Initiating rollback to stable model version rwd-bert-v3.1:
```
redwood rollout rollback --deployment chat-service --to-version rwd-bert-v3.1-stable
```
oncall-bot: Rollback job started at 14:22 UTC; ETA ~4m.
rachel: After rollback completes, p99 back to ~480ms, p95 ~420ms across regions. Streaming back to expected behavior.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260215-17 updated: mitigation applied, traffic normalized. Monitoring window: 1h.
sre-lead: Good containment. Postmortem owner: @luis. Action items: timeline, kernel selector guardrail, canary weight auto-rollback threshold.
alex: Leaving logs and quick timeline in the incident doc, handing off to @oncall-handoff for watch.
oncall-handoff: Acknowledged. I'll own watches and updates to CS for the next 60m. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
